items.justification: Automatic update activation on the device versus rate limiting on an externally exposed model API.
Vulnerability monitoring and incident/recovery planning are separate processes that jointly make up post-market security response.
Physical interface exposure on a device versus an organizational review of access control frameworks for AI assets; B never names hardware interfaces.
Cryptographic strength of authentication versus the risk of models carrying unused functionality.
Erasure capability and disclosure of how data is used are different obligations that together form user control over personal data.
Per-device uniqueness of security parameters and proportionate protection of model weights both serve protection of confidential assets, from different ends.
Recording justifications for non-applicable provisions versus tailoring disaster recovery to AI-specific attacks.
Hardware memory access control versus publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy.
Both require secure deletion of data; A adds user confirmation, B adds the decommissioning trigger and configuration details.
Both govern how updates are handled securely; A mandates the automatic mechanism, B mandates re-testing after a major update.
User guidance on verifying secure setup versus due diligence on external AI components.
Both require accessible user-facing guidance; A is confined to data deletion, B to system use and configuration.
Encryption of security parameters in transit and proportionate protection of confidential training assets protect different material under one confidentiality control.
Disabling debug interfaces versus maintaining an audit trail for models and datasets.
Timeliness of security updates versus justifying the use of poorly documented model components.
Detecting unauthorized change to device software versus sanitising training data and inputs; different integrity problems with no single control joining them.
Orderly network reconnection versus threat modelling on configuration change; the process text does not name network behaviour.
Lifecycle management of critical security parameters versus technical measures supporting human oversight.
Update timeliness versus recording the provenance of scraped training data.
Setup guidance for consumers versus access protection for training and test data.
Both require accessible advance communication about update status; A covers absence of updates and replacement support, B covers planned model updates.
Uniqueness of device security parameters versus threat modelling triggered by configuration change.
Secure development process and lifecycle threat modelling are distinct processes that jointly constitute a secure development lifecycle.
Local operation during network loss versus secure software supply chain processes.
A mandates the secure development process, B the developer competence it depends on; together they form one secure development programme.
Verifying update authenticity versus limiting the permissions an AI system holds on connected systems.
Changing an authentication value versus sharing documentation with End-users.
Deletion instructions for consumers versus asset tracking and version control for AI artefacts.
Password use in machine-to-machine authentication versus separation of development and tuning environments.
Management of critical security parameters versus supporting End-users through an incident.
Acting on disclosed vulnerabilities versus documenting the provenance of public training data.
Secure development of the manufacturer's own software versus justifying reliance on third-party components.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus user guidance on system configuration.
Changing an authentication value versus matching intended system usage to data sensitivity.
Resilience to power and network outages versus informing users of prohibited use cases.
Remediating disclosed vulnerabilities and communicating unresolved threats downstream are the two halves of coordinated vulnerability handling.
Disabling unnecessary software services versus notifying users of security-relevant updates.
Code minimization versus documenting the origin of public training data.
User control over automatic updates versus awareness of prohibited use cases.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus risk assessment of external AI components.
